This notebook runs the same checks as `run_spatialdata_e2e.sh`, stage by stage,
and shows what each stage produced. It needs the `spatialdata` python package and a
built `punkst` binary (set the `PUNKST` environment variable, or build to
`<repo>/bin/punkst`).

## Setup

```{python}
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, warnings
from pathlib import Path

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.collections import PatchCollection
from matplotlib.patches import RegularPolygon

here = Path.cwd()
sys.path.insert(0, str(here))
sys.path.insert(0, str(here.parent))
from make_synthetic_sdata import build, build_structured
from spatialdata_to_punkst import convert

punkst = Path(os.environ.get("PUNKST", here.parents[2] / "bin" / "punkst"))
assert punkst.exists(), f"punkst binary not found at {punkst}; set PUNKST"
work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="punkst_sd_"))

def run(*args):
    """Run a punkst subcommand, raising with its output on failure."""
    r = subprocess.run([str(punkst), *map(str, args)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(r.stdout + r.stderr)
    return r

print("punkst:", punkst)
print("work dir:", work)
```

## 1. Converter: coordinate systems

The small fixture registers its points in two coordinate systems: `pixels`
(identity) and `microns` (a scale by 2). The converter must apply the chosen
transform, and must refuse to guess when more than one system is registered.

```{python}
truth = build(str(work / "synthetic.zarr"), n_points=500, scale=2.0, seed=11)

try:
    convert(str(work / "synthetic.zarr"), "transcripts", str(work / "amb.tsv"))
except ValueError as e:
    print("ambiguous coordinate system correctly rejected:\n ", e)

convert(str(work / "synthetic.zarr"), "transcripts", str(work / "microns.tsv"),
        coordinate_system="microns")
convert(str(work / "synthetic.zarr"), "transcripts", str(work / "pixels.tsv"),
        coordinate_system="pixels")

mic = pd.read_csv(work / "microns.tsv", sep="\t", comment="#", header=None,
                  names=["x", "y", "feature"])
pix = pd.read_csv(work / "pixels.tsv", sep="\t", comment="#", header=None,
                  names=["x", "y", "feature"])
assert len(mic) == 500
np.testing.assert_allclose(
    mic.sort_values(["x", "y"]).x.values / 2,
    pix.sort_values(["x", "y"]).x.values, atol=1e-3)
print(open(work / "microns.tsv").readline().rstrip(), "(header)")
mic.head()
```

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.6), sharex=False)
for a, d, t in [(ax[0], pix, "pixels (identity)"), (ax[1], mic, "microns (scale 2)")]:
    a.scatter(d.x, d.y, s=4, alpha=.6)
    a.set_title(t); a.set_aspect("equal"); a.set_xlabel("x"); a.set_ylabel("y")
fig.tight_layout()
```

The same molecules land at twice the coordinates in the `microns` system, so the
SpatialData transformation is being applied on export.

## 2. Structured fixture

Now a fixture with real structure: the left half of the tissue is enriched for
the `A*` genes and the right half for the `B*` genes. A 2-topic model should
recover this.

```{python}
build_structured(str(work / "structured.zarr"), seed=5)
convert(str(work / "structured.zarr"), "transcripts", str(work / "st.tsv"))
st = pd.read_csv(work / "st.tsv", sep="\t", comment="#", header=None,
                 names=["x", "y", "feature"])
st["group"] = st.feature.str[0]
print(f"{len(st):,} molecules, {st.feature.nunique()} genes")

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4.6))
sub = st.sample(15000, random_state=0)
for g, c in [("A", "tab:red"), ("B", "tab:blue")]:
    d = sub[sub.group == g]
    ax.scatter(d.x, d.y, s=1.5, alpha=.5, c=c, label=f"{g}* genes")
ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.legend(markerscale=6)
ax.set_title("Transcripts exported from SpatialData")
```

## 3. `pts2tiles`

```{python}
run("pts2tiles", "--in-tsv", work / "st.tsv",
    "--icol-x", 0, "--icol-y", 1, "--icol-feature", 2,
    "--tile-size", 100, "--temp-dir", work / "tmp1",
    "--out-prefix", work / "st.tiled")
for suffix in ("tsv", "index", "features.tsv"):
    f = work / f"st.tiled.{suffix}"
    assert f.stat().st_size > 0
    print(f"{f.name:22s} {f.stat().st_size:>10,} bytes")
```

## 4. `tiles2hex`

```{python}
run("tiles2hex", "--in-tsv", work / "st.tiled.tsv", "--in-index", work / "st.tiled.index",
    "--feature-dict", work / "st.tiled.features.tsv",
    "--icol-x", 0, "--icol-y", 1, "--icol-feature", 2,
    "--hex-grid-dist", 12, "--min-count", 5,
    "--out", work / "hex.txt", "--randomize", "--seed", 1,
    "--temp-dir", work / "tmp2")
hist = pd.read_csv(work / "hex.count_hist.tsv", sep="\t", header=None)
n_hex = sum(1 for _ in open(work / "hex.txt"))
print(n_hex, "hexagons")
hist.head()
```

## 5. `topic-model`

```{python}
run("topic-model", "--in-data", work / "hex.txt", "--in-meta", work / "hex.json",
    "--features", work / "st.tiled.features.tsv",
    "--n-topics", 2, "--n-epochs", 5, "--min-count-train", 5,
    "--out-prefix", work / "lda", "--transform", "--threads", 2, "--seed", 1)

model = pd.read_csv(work / "lda.model.tsv", sep="\t", index_col=0)
frac_a = [model.loc[model.index.str.startswith("A"), k].sum() / model[k].sum()
          for k in model.columns]
print("A-gene fraction per topic:", [round(f, 3) for f in frac_a])
assert max(frac_a) > 0.7 and min(frac_a) < 0.3, "topics did not separate A/B genes"
```

### Topic–gene loadings

Each column is normalised to a distribution over genes. One topic should
concentrate on `A*` genes and the other on `B*`.

```{python}
norm = model / model.sum()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 5))
im = ax.imshow(norm.values, aspect="auto", cmap="viridis")
ax.set_yticks(range(len(norm))); ax.set_yticklabels(norm.index, fontsize=7)
ax.set_xticks(range(norm.shape[1])); ax.set_xticklabels([f"topic {k}" for k in norm.columns])
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label="P(gene | topic)")
fig.tight_layout()
```

### Topics in space

Each hexagon is coloured by its probability of the topic that loads on `A*`
genes. It should split the tissue at x = 100, matching how the data were
generated.

```{python}
res = pd.read_csv(work / "lda.results.tsv", sep="\t")
res = res.rename(columns={"#random_key": "key"})
a_topic = str(int(np.argmax(frac_a)))
hex_dist = 12
side = hex_dist / np.sqrt(3)  # side length of a hexagon with this center spacing

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.5, 4.4))
for ax, col, title in [(axs[0], a_topic, f"P(topic {a_topic})  [A*-dominated]"),
                       (axs[1], None, "Top topic")]:
    patches = [RegularPolygon((x, y), 6, radius=side, orientation=0)
               for x, y in zip(res.x, res.y)]
    pc = PatchCollection(patches, edgecolor="none")
    if col is not None:
        pc.set_array(res[col].values); pc.set_cmap("coolwarm"); pc.set_clim(0, 1)
    else:
        pc.set_array(res[["0", "1"]].values.argmax(axis=1)); pc.set_cmap("tab10"); pc.set_clim(0, 9)
    ax.add_collection(pc)
    ax.set_xlim(0, 200); ax.set_ylim(0, 200); ax.set_aspect("equal"); ax.set_title(title)
    if col is not None:
        fig.colorbar(pc, ax=ax, fraction=.046)
fig.tight_layout()

left = res[res.x < 90]; right = res[res.x > 110]
print(f"mean P(topic {a_topic}): left half {left[a_topic].mean():.2f}, right half {right[a_topic].mean():.2f}")
assert left[a_topic].mean() > 0.8 and right[a_topic].mean() < 0.2
```
